title: External Attack Surface Management (EASM) Foundation
goal: Add passive external discovery that automatically maps an organisation's attack surface from a domain name — subdomains, IPs, exposed services, technology stack — before the operator has to manually specify targets.
scope: Implement an 'easm-discover' runner in workers/runners/easm/ that performs read-only passive reconnaissance from a root domain: (1) Subdomain enumeration using subfinder (already available on Kali) or DNS brute-force with a curated wordlist; (2) DNS resolution and ASN lookup for discovered subdomains; (3) HTTP fingerprinting of live hosts using httpx (already in stack) to detect status codes, titles, technology stack; (4) Certificate transparency log query (crt.sh JSON API — no key required) for additional subdomain discovery; (5) Results feed into inventory snapshots as easm-class assets distinct from operator-seeded scope. A new 'passive-easm-discovery' run profile is added. The operator provides only a root domain (e.g. example.com) — the runner discovers the full external footprint. Discovered assets are presented in Surface Map with an 'Add to scope' option — they are not automatically added to active scan scope. This enables Hadrian/Pentera-style 'give us your domain, we find everything' positioning.
generation_reason: External Attack Surface Management is one of the fastest-growing segments in offensive security. Pentera, NodeZero, and dedicated EASM tools (Hadrian, Censys, Shodan) all offer automated external discovery. AegisPT currently requires the operator to manually specify every target. EASM lets an operator provide just a domain name and see their full external footprint before deciding what to test — matching how real assessments start.

constraints.active_task_gate: Do not implement this task until it is the single active task in NEXT_TASK.md.
constraints.scope_creep_guard: Passive discovery only — no active probing beyond HTTP fingerprinting. Discovered assets require explicit operator approval before being added to active scan scope. crt.sh queries are the only external API call — no paid EASM services required. DNS brute-force uses a bounded wordlist (max 10,000 entries).

success_criteria: easm-discover runner enumerates subdomains from a root domain using subfinder/DNS and crt.sh.
Discovered assets are stored as easm-class inventory snapshots.
Surface Map displays discovered assets with 'Add to scope' option.
Discovered assets are NOT automatically added to active scan scope.
crt.sh is the only external API call.
Tests cover discovery, inventory storage, scope non-expansion, and Surface Map rendering.
must_not_touch: Automatic scope expansion from discovered assets
pack registry, validation, approval, deployment, or runtime binding flows

acceptance_criteria: Runner discovers subdomains and stores as EASM inventory.
Surface Map shows discovered assets with Add to scope option.

before_promotion: Burp Suite runner integration (backlog-66) is completed and logged.
after_completion: Update DONE_LOG.md with EASM runner implementation.
Update CURRENT_STATE.md with EASM discovery as active capability.
Promote exactly one next approved task package into NEXT_TASK.md, or set an explicit holding state if the queue is exhausted.

out_of_scope: Port scanning of discovered assets (nmap runner handles this after scope approval)
